heroHeadline: Egypt's Foreign Reserves Hit Record $55B as Sisi Outlines Post-IMF Plan; Cairo Hosts Gaza Phase-Two Talks; Egypt Declares GERD Talks at an Impasse
heroSubtitle: Egypt's Central Bank reported net foreign reserves surpassing $55 billion for the first time on July 16, 2026, a record milestone Prime Minister Madbouly attributed to strong exports, tourism, and remittances — even as he acknowledged ordinary citizens have yet to feel the benefit. The reserves record came days after President Sisi inaugurated a new State Strategic Command in the New Administrative Capital on July 4 and directed preparation of a homegrown economic programme to follow the current IMF loan's conclusion. On the diplomatic front, Egyptian, Israeli, and Hamas delegations met in Cairo July 9–11 to salvage the stalled second phase of the Gaza ceasefire, while Sisi made a Gulf solidarity tour to Qatar and Bahrain on July 14 amid expanded US strikes on Iran. Egypt also hardened its position on the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, with Foreign Minister Abdelatty declaring negotiations with Ethiopia at an impasse and warning against further unilateral Blue Nile dam construction. Archaeologically, Egyptian missions uncovered new sections of a 26th-Dynasty temple at Bahariya Oasis and two Early Dynastic-era tombs at Gabal El-Teir in Minya.
footerNote: Data sourced from Egyptian official records, UNESCO, academic Egyptology research (Shaw, Lehner, Hawass), major international outlets, IMF, Human Rights Watch, and institutional analyses.
